Keep SAF files out of a project's git commits

Source: R/use_srtr_protections.R
use_srtr_gitignore.Rd

Two opt-in helpers for your own analysis project. Each writes only inside the project folder you give it.

  • use_srtr_gitignore() adds patterns for the file formats SAFs come in (.sas7bdat, .sas7bcat, .xpt, .parquet, .feather, .arrow, .dta, .sav, in any letter case) to the project's .gitignore, creating the file if needed. Patterns already there are not added again.

  • use_srtr_commit_check() installs a git pre-commit hook that runs check_repo_for_srtr_data() on the files staged for each commit and stops the commit when it finds any that look like SRTR data. It will not replace a pre-commit hook it did not write.

Usage

use_srtr_gitignore(path)

use_srtr_commit_check(path)

Arguments

path

The project folder. There is no default: these functions change files in the folder you name. For use_srtr_commit_check(), the folder must be inside a git repository; the hook is installed for that repository.

Value

The path of the file written, invisibly.

Limits

The .gitignore patterns catch the usual SAF formats only: not .rds, .RData or .csv files made from a SAF, and git add -f overrides them.

The commit hook lives in the project's own .git folder, so it is not copied when someone clones the project; each person runs use_srtr_commit_check() in their own copy. git commit --no-verify skips it. It checks each staged file as it was staged, even when the copy in the folder has changed since. It needs Rscript on the path that git uses and sRtr installed in that R; if either is missing, it stops the commit and says so. On Windows, Git for Windows runs the hook with its own shell, so check once that a commit with a made-up .sas7bdat file is stopped.

None of this makes a repository a safe place for SRTR data, and a private repository is still a disclosure. See the data protection guide.

See also

Other data protection: check_repo_for_srtr_data()

Examples

project <- file.path(tempdir(), "made-up-project")
dir.create(project, showWarnings = FALSE)
use_srtr_gitignore(project)
#> ✔ Added 8 SAF patterns to .gitignore:
#>   /tmp/RtmprydEfS/made-up-project/.gitignore
#> ℹ Files git already tracks stay tracked; remove them with `git rm --cached
#>   <file>`.
readLines(file.path(project, ".gitignore"))
#> [1] "# SRTR data: never commit (added by sRtr::use_srtr_gitignore())"
#> [2] "*.[sS][aA][sS]7[bB][dD][aA][tT]"                                
#> [3] "*.[sS][aA][sS]7[bB][cC][aA][tT]"                                
#> [4] "*.[xX][pP][tT]"                                                 
#> [5] "*.[pP][aA][rR][qQ][uU][eE][tT]"                                 
#> [6] "*.[fF][eE][aA][tT][hH][eE][rR]"                                 
#> [7] "*.[aA][rR][rR][oO][wW]"                                         
#> [8] "*.[dD][tT][aA]"                                                 
#> [9] "*.[sS][aA][vV]"                                                 

# A second call adds nothing.
use_srtr_gitignore(project)
#> ✔ .gitignore already has sRtr's SAF patterns:
#>   /tmp/RtmprydEfS/made-up-project/.gitignore

unlink(project, recursive = TRUE)
